title: Points isolated in their fibre stay isolated after base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $g:S'\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, and let $X'=X\times_SS'$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$. Let $x'\in X'$, and put $x=g'(x')$, $s'=f'(x')$, $s=f(x)=g(s')$. If $x$ is an isolated point of the fibre $X_s$ of $f$ at $s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] (the singleton is open in $X_s$), then $x'$ is an isolated point of the fibre $X'_{s'}=X'\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')$ of $f'$ at $s'$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01TM (morphisms-lemma-base-change-quasi-finite, line 3925), part (1), combined with Lemma 01TH (morphisms-lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize, line 3664), (1) <=> (2); used in the proof of More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LM (more-morphisms.tex lines 12079-12081)

proof.text: Fibre of the base change. Let $r:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s')$ be the map induced by $g$ on residue fields. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change] there is a morphism $h:X'_{s'}\to X_s$ with $\iota\circ h=g'\circ\iota'$ (where $\iota:X_s\to X$, $\iota':X'_{s'}\to X'$ are the first projections) which, together with the projection $X'_{s'}\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')$, makes $X'_{s'}$ a fibre product $X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ being $\operatorname{Spec}(r)$. Since $f'(x')=s'$, by [def-pc-scheme-fibre] there is a unique point $\xi'\in X'_{s'}$ with $\iota'(\xi')=x'$; this is the point of the fibre meant by '$x'$ is isolated in $X'_{s'}$'. Put $\xi=h(\xi')$. Then $\iota(\xi)=g'(\iota'(\xi'))=g'(x')=x$, and since $\iota$ is injective (a homeomorphism onto $f^{-1}(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]), $\xi$ is the point of $X_s$ corresponding to $x$; by hypothesis $\{\xi\}$ is open in $X_s$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00PP (algebra-lemma-quasi-finite-base-change, line 30362), first sentence ('the fibre ring S' (x)_{R'} kappa(p') is the base change of the fibre ring S (x)_R kappa(p) by the field extension kappa(p) -> kappa(p')'), in its scheme form Morphisms, proof of Lemma 02V4 (morphisms.tex line 7381)

proof.text: The open point as a scheme over $\kappa(s)$. Let $W\subseteq X_s$ be the open subscheme with underlying set $\{\xi\}$ and $w:W\to X_s$ its inclusion, an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. The morphism $w$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] (2); the projection $\pi:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is the base change of the morphism $f$, locally of finite type, along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$, hence locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]; so $\pi\circ w:W\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e). The underlying space of $W$ is one point, hence discrete.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemmas 01T5 (lemma-immersion-locally-finite-type), 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type), 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type); the finite type hypothesis of Algebra, Lemma 00PP

proof.text: Base change of the open point is discrete and open. By [lem-weil-pbc-discrete-field-base-change-artinian] (with $k=\kappa(s)$, $K=\kappa(s')$ via $r$, and the scheme $W$ of the previous step), the base change $W_{\kappa(s')}=W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')$ has discrete underlying space. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], applied to the fibre product $X'_{s'}=X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')$ of the first step with the opens $W\subseteq X_s$, $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')$, the canonical morphism $W_{\kappa(s')}\to X'_{s'}$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] with image $h^{-1}(W)$. Hence $h^{-1}(W)$ is an open subset of $X'_{s'}$ and, being homeomorphic to $W_{\kappa(s')}$, is discrete in the subspace topology.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00PP (line 30362): 'the first assertion follows from the invariance of dimension under field extension (Lemma 00P4, lemma-dimension-at-a-point-preserved-field-extension) and Lemma 00PJ (lemma-isolated-point)', here in the case of dimension 0 at an isolated point, which is what [lem-weil-pbc-discrete-field-base-change-artinian] states

proof.text: Conclusion. Since $h(\xi')=\xi\in W$, $\xi'\in h^{-1}(W)$. As $h^{-1}(W)$ is discrete, $\{\xi'\}$ is open in $h^{-1}(W)$, and as $h^{-1}(W)$ is open in $X'_{s'}$, $\{\xi'\}$ is open in $X'_{s'}$: $x'$ is an isolated point of $X'_{s'}$.

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks Morphisms 01TM (1) (line 3925) with 01TH (1)<=>(2) (line 3664): correct as stated (the 'point x'' of the fibre is the point of X'_{s'} over x'; made explicit in step 1). Stacks proves 01TM (1) through affine opens (01TH (4)) and Algebra 00PP (line 30362), whose proof is: the fibre of the base change is the base change of the fibre by kappa(p) -> kappa(p'), and isolatedness (dimension 0, 00P4 + 00PJ) is preserved by field extension. The split runs that argument directly on the scheme fibres, avoiding quasi-finiteness: (1) X'_{s'} = X_s x_{kappa(s)} kappa(s') (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change = isPullback_fiberToSpecResidueField_of_isPullback, Fiber.lean:65; Stacks states it in the proofs of 02V3/02V4); (2) the open point W = {x} of X_s is lft over kappa(s) (existing leaves 01T5, 01T4, 01T3); (3) W_{kappa(s')} is discrete (existing leaf lem-weil-pbc-discrete-field-base-change-artinian, 00P4 case dim 0) and is the open h^{-1}(W) of X'_{s'} (existing leaf lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product, 01JR); (4) topology. No Mathlib declaration for the item at scheme level (searches added). One new node, a Mathlib leaf. Tags verified in tags/tags: 01TM, 01TH, 00PP, 00P4, 00PJ, 02V3, 02V4, 01T3, 01T4, 01T5, 01JR. The brief's guesses 00PM/00PL/00PN/01TG for base change were wrong: the algebra lemma is 00PP (00PL is the definition of quasi-finite, 01TG is lemma-residue-field-quasi-finite).
